title: Copilot Agent in AL: Using It Well Without Losing Control
summary: Copilot Agent works at a task level across multiple AL objects and files, unlike Chat or Edit which work on single selections. It works best when used as a guided collaborator with explicit constraints, clear scope, and incremental steps rather than as an autonomous solution builder.
key_points: Copilot Agent interprets input as a goal and creates or modifies code across multiple files to reach it, which differs fundamentally from Chat, Ask, or Edit that operate locally on single selections

Agent works most effectively when scope is clear, tasks are incremental, and architectural intent is explicit, used to scaffold features and implement pre-made decisions rather than solve complex business logic

Using Agent successfully requires treating it as a collaborative process with narrow tasks, output review, constraints reinforcement, and continuous refinement rather than expecting autonomous completion
AL's opinionated patterns mean Agent can produce technically valid but architecturally misaligned code if developer intent is not explicitly reinforced throughout the process
Common pitfalls include too many objects, inconsistent naming, and logic in wrong layers, which become more visible when Agent operates across files

quotes.text: Copilot Agent works best when it is treated as a guided collaborator, not as an autonomous solution builder.
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes the core mental model for using Agent effectively, shifting expectations from autonomy to guided task implementation

quotes.text: Agent optimises for task completion. Architectural correctness still depends on the developer.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies that Agent is a tool for acceleration, not a replacement for architectural decision-making or validation

quotes.text: In AL development, structure and intent matter too much to be left implicit.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains why explicit constraints and boundaries are essential when using Agent in AL projects
